newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower in line with Dow retreat.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower in line with Dow retreat.

text.p: Italian stocks ended just off session lows after a dull session on Thursday. Traders said the market was entirely driven by external factors, moving lower as Wall Street stocks retreated from an early rally and depressed by profit-taking on the debt market.

After starting mixed in thin, directionless trade, the Milan bourse rose after U.S. data indicated a slowdown in growth and therefore less inflationary pressure, only to slip as Dow industrials backtracked.
The All-share Mibtel index ended off 0.65 percent at 10,160 after a 10,156-10,266 range and the Mib30 blue chip index was down 0.7 percent at 15,116 after a 15,111-15,314 range.

Energy group ENI ended 0.84 percent easier at 7,635 lire, Fiat lost 0.88 percent to 4,275, Olivetti slipped 0.23 percent to 516 and Pirelli & C holding company shed 2.65 percent to 1,875. Media group Mediaset lost 1.02 percent to 6,995 lire.
Telecoms were mixed with mobile phone operator TIM down 2.09 percent to 3,510 lire, but Telecom Italia put on 0.35 percent to 3,465 and holding company Stet gained 0.52 percent to 6,220.
Carlo De Benedetti's financial holding company Cofide dropped 6.23 percent to 825 lire but his Cir industrial holding put on 0.49 percent to 962.

Some dealers cited the war of words over economic forecasts for the country between Italy's employers' body Confindustria and the centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi as weighing on overall sentiment.
"The market is still a bit timorous. A rebound on the Italian stock market had appeared possible but Wall Street's poor performance snuffed out any such vain ambitions," one trader said.
